data.content_ref: inline:SRC_003 contradicts SRC_002 over the dominant cross-city predictor of nocturnal UHI magnitude: SRC_003 claims scaling with built density / impervious surface fraction via thermal mass, while SRC_002 claims scaling with green-space / vegetation fraction via latent-heat deficit. These are in direct tension because increasing impervious surface (SRC_003's predictor) simultaneously decreases vegetation (SRC_002's predictor), making the two predictors mechanistically anti-correlated and statistically confounded. This contradiction is REFUTED IF a controlled cross-city study finds that, when holding impervious-fraction constant, varying vegetation cover still independently predicts UHI magnitude (which would integrate, rather than contradict, the two mechanisms), or conversely if holding vegetation constant, varying thermal mass still independently predicts UHI.
